text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- JERUSALEM POST
- Jordan's King Hussein rebukes Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in letter.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton: Har Homa veto isn't approval.
- Prime minister's adviser on Druse affairs, Assad Assad, says his people shouldn't have to be government "shabbes goys".
- Mutual fund assets up 13 percent since January.
- Transport Ministry director-general says El Al Israel Airlines to be sold within a month.
- Blue Square posts 22 percent rise in annual net profits.
GLOBES
- Morgan Stanley buys about 9 percent stake in Koor Industries for 130-150 million dollars.
- Revlon closes its factory in Israel.
- Shaul Eisenberg and Volkswagen in first negotiations for joint purchase from Israel of shares in Israel Chemicals.
- For the first time in two years negative amassing of wealth in index-linked savings accounts.
HAARETZ

- Grave crisis between Israel and Palestinians. President Yasser Arafat spurns appeals by Netanyahu. Redeployment delayed "because there's no one to receive the territory". Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai tells Palestinian negotiator Yasser Abed Rabbo that Har Homa settlement will be built as planned.
- Delays in takeoffs and landings of planes at Ben-Gurion Airport following pirate radio broadcasts.
- Russian military industry officials to Damascus to discuss sale of arms and military supplies.
- Government opposes bill to deny president authority to ease punishment of Yitzhak Rabin's assassin Yigal Amir.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- King Hussein warns Netanyahu in secret message of potential blow-up of peace process.
- Five directors of Africa-Israel want board of directors to convene on "sabbath affair" at Ramat Aviv mall.
- Turkish beer Efes Pilsen in Israel soon.
MAARIV
- King Hussein to Netanyahu: I haven't a morsel of trust in you, voices anger at Netanyahu for barring him from flying Arafat to Gaza from Amman in royal plane.
- Is Sara Netanyahu pregnant? Netanyahu: I'll report when there will be something to report.
